title: Repayment Shape of a Temporary Rate Reduction Plan by Due Dates Left
content:
**Rule.** For a Temporary Rate Reduction Plan of the Hardship Assistance Programs, a loan with 12 or fewer due dates left from its next due date through its maturity date pays, on each plan due date, the principal part of its scheduled installment, being that installment less one month's interest on the unpaid principal at the loan's current rate and never below zero, plus one month's interest on the unpaid principal at the plan rate, so that the payment falls by exactly the interest the lower rate saves; a loan with more than 36 due dates left pays one month's interest on the unpaid principal at the plan rate and no principal; any other loan pays the level installment at the plan rate, the due dates left being the whole calendar months from the next due date to the maturity date plus one. The scheduled installment, the current rate, the unpaid principal and the dates are those on the loan's Personal Loans record; one month's interest is the unpaid principal multiplied by one-twelfth of the annual rate.

## Method table

| Due dates left | Plan installment |
|---|---|
| 12 or fewer | scheduled installment less one month's interest at the current rate (never below zero), plus one month's interest at the plan rate |
| 13 to 36 | level installment at the plan rate |
| more than 36 | one month's interest at the plan rate, no principal |

## Worked figures (hypothetical: unpaid principal 6,000.00 USD, scheduled installment 540.00 USD, current rate 18.00 percent, plan rate 6.00 percent)

- 10 due dates left: one month's interest at 18.00 percent is 90.00, so the principal part is 450.00; one month's interest at 6.00 percent is 30.00; plan installment 480.00 USD.
- 40 due dates left: one month's interest at 6.00 percent, 30.00 USD, and no principal.
